verbalization: Zidovudine is likely to interact with Slc22a2 through a mechanism involving the organic cation/anion/zwitterion transport system. The evidence suggests that Zidovudine binds to Slc22a11, which is part of this transport pathway, and Slc22a11 participates in the transport of organic cation/anion/zwitterions. Since Slc22a2 is a member of the same family of transporters, it is plausible that Zidovudine influences Slc22a2 through this shared functional pathway. The binding of Zidovudine to Slc22a11 may modulate the activity of Slc22a2, potentially affecting the transport of its substrates. This relationship is supported by the observed interaction between Zidovudine and Slc22a11, and the functional link between Slc22a11 and Slc22a2, suggesting a possible regulatory or competitive interaction at the transporter level.
